clue.text: For part of flight, loved animals going up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: animals kept and loved at home

explanation.surface: Pets carried up a staircase on part of a flight, or animals boarding a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of individual steps, so one step is a part of it.

clue.text: Other producer of pictures arrived before artist

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the finished word

parts.note: past tense of come
RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A rival picture-maker turned up before the painter did.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says 'other' because the clue has just mentioned an artist, the more obvious maker of pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is a device that takes photographs, a different producer of images from a painter.

clue.text: Introducer of the first palindrome?

parts.note: surface reading: the person who first came up with a phrase reading the same both ways
setter's reading: the first man, presenting himself to Eve in Eden with the traditional palindromic greeting

explanation.walkthrough: The traditional joke palindrome is the first man's greeting to Eve, 'Madam, I'm ...', so he introduced it while introducing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man greets the first woman, and the joke palindrome puts that greeting in his mouth.

clue.text: Princess and I very minimally raised capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal
taken as written

indicators.note: minimally keeps only the smallest possible part of the word, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of very

explanation.surface: A princess and the speaker lifted a city's status ever so slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Longing for perfection, I'm embracing ladies haphazardly

indicators.note: done haphazardly means done in no fixed order, so the letters are jumbled
embracing means wrapping around, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: taken as written, split around the jumble
the letters of ladies rearranged

explanation.surface: A man confesses he hugs women at random in his hunt for the ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the pursuit of perfect standards, a yearning for things as they ought to be.

clue.text: Historical military leader and PM in faraway capital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the duke who won at Waterloo and later became British prime minister
second meaning: the capital of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A famous general and premier turns up in a distant capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of New Zealand was named after the Duke, so the two meanings share a source.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon and was prime minister; New Zealand's capital, on the far side of the world, bears his title.

clue.text: Short of money, performed vocally on street

indicators.note: on places one piece next to the other, here the road abbreviation comes first

parts.note: standard abbreviation for street
delivered rhythmic spoken lyrics

explanation.surface: A broke busker sang on the street for coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash is an idiom for being hard up, lacking funds.

clue.text: Fended off Duke after changing rapier

indicators.note: changing the weapon's name means altering the order of its letters
after puts the title's abbreviation at the end, following the reworked letters

parts.note: the letters of rapier rearranged
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duelling duke blocked a thrust after switching swords.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry is to deflect an attack, so fended off is its past tense.

clue.text: Covered by legal document, actually

parts.note: something covered by a thing is in it
a deed is a signed legal instrument

explanation.surface: A claim that something really is included in the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb meaning in fact or truly, a synonym for actually.

clue.text: Hearing organ after a couple of pianos in show

indicators.note: after places the listening organ at the end, behind the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
p is the musical marking for piano, so two of them
the organ we hear with

explanation.surface: A musician listens after a pair of keyboard instruments in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano here is the musical direction for softly, abbreviated p.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to appear, become visible or turn up.

clue.text: Male friend grabbing you, as stated, by hand

indicators.note: grabbing means holding onto, so the friend wraps around the sound-alike letter

parts.note: a male person
a supporter or partner

indicators.note: as stated means as it is spoken, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A man's mate seizes the listener, physically, with his hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Manually means done with the hands rather than by machine.

clue.text: Creating classes in summer term, initially, with formal consent

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two preceding words

parts.note: the first letters of summer and term
ratification is formal approval, as of a treaty

explanation.surface: A school sets up new classes during the summer term with official approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classes' looks like school lessons, but the definition means social or geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratification is arrangement into layers or ranks, so it creates social classes or strata.

clue.text: Kind of policies for political group outside mainstream

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a basic level of motor insurance cover
second meaning: a party other than the two main ones

explanation.surface: A fringe party's manifesto commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policies' looks political, but in the first meaning they are insurance policies, the legal minimum cover for drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-party insurance covers damage to others; a third party is a minor political force beyond the two main ones.

clue.text: Make a deduction that's popular — reduced payment, right?

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: in fashion, popular
a charge paid for a service
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An accountant's question about whether a popular discounted charge counts as a tax deduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deduction' suggests subtracting money, but the definition is about reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning, which is to deduce.

clue.text: Desire exists between married couple

indicators.note: between puts one piece in the middle with the other on each side

parts.note: wife and husband, W and H, which go on either side
is means exists

explanation.surface: A longing sits between husband and wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish is a want or longing, a synonym for desire.

clue.text: Dithering husband in state, confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the letters of in state rearranged

explanation.surface: A spouse is in a muddled, flustered condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In state' looks like the husband is inside a condition, but those two words are the letters to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant means unsure and slow to act, which is what dithering describes.

clue.text: Author, in awe of editor, held back

indicators.note: held back means turned backwards, so the concealed letters read right to left
in says the word lies inside the letters of the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of awe, of and the start of editor

explanation.surface: A writer, overawed by his editor, kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, so he is an author.

clue.text: For example, rising embraced by primitive with enthusiasm

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the short piece goes within the longer word

parts.note: early in development, primitive

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: An example of something ascending, wrapped up in early forms, keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly means keenly or zealously, doing something with enthusiasm.

clue.text: What queen might do to king or consort

definitions.text: What queen might do to king
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in chess, trap the king so the game ends
second meaning: a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A royal question: what a queen does to her king, or to her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The royals look like a married couple, but the first meaning is a chess move delivered by the queen piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmating is often shortened in chess; and a consort is a spouse, a partner one pairs with.

clue.text: Record how old we are — intended, we hear, as deterrent

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for the act or thing that puts off

parts.note: a gramophone record
our age, the years we have lived

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spelt by its sound rather than as written

parts.note: meant, intended, sounds like the suffix

explanation.surface: Logging our ages, meant to put people off.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement is something that puts people off doing a thing, much like a deterrent.

clue.text: Harangued and scolded after worst possible score

indicators.note: after places the scolding word behind the score in the final order

parts.note: zero, nil, the lowest score
rate is an old verb meaning to scold angrily

explanation.surface: A team was shouted at and told off after scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rate meaning scold is an old word, still alive in the noun berating.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a speech, often pompously; harangued means delivered a long forceful speech.

clue.text: Spirits, including last of rum — or beer

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of rum
taken as written
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A pub order of strong drink, including the dregs of the rum, or a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like strong liquor beside rum and beer, but it means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence or mood of a group, their spirits being high or low.

clue.text: Sliced beef pie, say, cut by friend in Paris

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a pie is an example of pastry
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A deli menu: beef pie, served by a French friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, spiced beef usually served thinly sliced in sandwiches.

clue.text: Doing nothing and indulged, oddly

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions, first, third and so on

parts.note: letters one, three, five and seven of indulged

explanation.surface: Lazing about and spoilt, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive or not working, which is doing nothing.

clue.text: A river contained by bank? Far from always

indicators.note: contained by means held within, so the first pair sits inside the second word

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
A taken as written plus R for river

explanation.surface: A river held within its banks, but by no means always.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a riverbank beside the river, but it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, the opposite of always, so it is far from always.

clue.text: Suffered beating — those expelled get it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: was defeated in a game or contest
second meaning: what people sent away are told to get, as in the dismissive phrase

explanation.surface: Pupils who took a beating were then thrown out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is cryptic: someone being thrown out is told to 'get ...', so they get the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten is to be defeated; and 'get lost!' is an idiom for a rude dismissal.

clue.text: Make amends about first of crimes immediately

indicators.note: about means around, so the atoning word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: to atone is to make up for a wrong

indicators.note: first of keeps only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of crimes

explanation.surface: An instruction to make up for one's crimes without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is an idiom meaning straight away, without any delay.

clue.text: Converted to ally, is steadfast supporter

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone won over to an alliance becomes a firm backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist stays faithful to a cause or ruler, a firm and unwavering backer.
